_variant_note:
Axis-1 for a nested-object write: turn off international online payments, confirm first.

The get_card_details read IS required here as of D2. The note this replaces argued the opposite — that set_card_controls' declared prerequisite was "never communicated to the model (to_openai_schema sends name/description/parameters only)", so requiring it would grade an undisclosed norm. That was true then and is false now: the model-facing description folds prerequisites in and says "Call get_card_details before this tool". The doctrine did not change, the disclosure did.

The payload shape is deliberately NOT pinned. arg_gate fixes card_id only, because the contract says 'only provided fields change; omitted fields keep their current values' — so a minimal partial ({online: {international: {enabled: false}}}) and a fuller echo are both correct, and pinning either would fail a valid call. What must not happen is touching a channel the customer never mentioned; with the outcome_merged mock the returned controls now show such a change instead of hiding it.

setup.persona: 24-year-old male, Supervisor and Foreman, Brewing, Aerated Water and Beverage Making, rural Purnia, Bihar

user_turns.content: I keep reading about card fraud on foreign websites. Please turn off international online payments on my credit card — I don't shop on overseas sites.
Yes, that's exactly what I want. Please do it.

get_card_details._comment: online.international is currently ENABLED with a 25000 limit — this is what must be turned off. Every other channel/region stays as-is.

set_card_controls._comment: The returned controls are COMPUTED: the card's current state from get_card_details with this call's payload merged in. A fixed reply could only assert the intended end state, so an over-broad write — touching a channel the customer never mentioned — came back looking as though it had not happened, and a model reporting faithfully from that reply looked correct. Within a run the state persists, so a second call sees the first.

get_card_details._comment: Required, and disclosed: this tool's description says "Call get_card_details before this tool". Without the read the assistant can only act on the customer's stated premise, and in cards that premise is wrong often enough to cause unnecessary or doomed state changes — a freeze on an already-frozen card, an unfreeze on a blocked one, a block on a card that has already expired. card_ids is deliberately NOT pinned: `required` compares by exact equality (grader.py:216) and for a list that is order-sensitive, so pinning it would fail a model that reads all of the customer's cards — a natural and correct move, especially where more than one card is in play. A1 enforces that the read happens, A4 that it happens first, and S1 that the ids are real.

set_card_controls._comment: Only card_id is pinned. The tool's own contract is 'Only provided fields change; omitted fields keep their current values' / 'Omit to leave unchanged' — so a MINIMAL PARTIAL (online.international.enabled=false alone) is the documented, canonical call, and a full controls echo with the one value flipped is equally correct. Both achieve the identical outcome, so pinning either shape would fail a correct call on wording rather than on the decision — exactly what ARCHITECTURE.md forbids. The semantic requirement (only international ONLINE goes off; domestic online and the other channels stay untouched) is therefore carried by the R bar, not by a nested arg match.

arg_gate._comment: toggle_card_freeze / block_card must not be called — the customer asked for a control change, not a freeze or block. Calling either fails A2.

calculate_rd_maturity._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

get_account_details._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks to turn off international online payments. The assistant should propose the change, confirm it (set_card_controls requires confirmation), and call set_card_controls setting online.international.enabled to false while leaving every other channel/region untouched — notably online.domestic must REMAIN enabled (the customer still shops on Indian sites), and ATM/POS must not be collaterally disabled. It should then report accurately what changed, grounded in the returned controls. Reading the current settings first via get_card_details is good practice and perfectly acceptable, but is NOT required and its absence is not a failure — the card_id is already known from login_context and partial updates are valid per the tool's contract. Disabling more than asked, or writing before confirming (S2), are the failures.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant confirms with the customer and turns off ONLY international online payments — leaving domestic online (and ATM/POS) untouched — then reports the change accurately from the tool's returned controls. Reading current settings first via get_card_details is optional and its absence must NOT be penalised. Disabling domestic online or other channels, acting before confirming, or claiming a change the tool output doesn't support fails.
